<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

Make expiring, refreshable tokens the default for `gh auth login`. Use `--no-expiring` to opt out. `--expiring` becomes a deprecated no-op, including `--expiring=false`.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I built both versions with `make` (passed) and ran `gh auth login --web --clipboard=false --insecure-storage` through `ghmock`. I used synthetic OAuth responses and isolated configuration. A sandbox blocked keyring access and external network connections.

I observed whether device authorization requested the `offline_access` scope for refresh tokens. Each listed login exited 0.

| Version and additional options | Requested `offline_access` |
| --- | --- |
| Base, default | No |
| Changed, default | Yes |
| Changed, `--no-expiring` | No |
| Changed, `--expiring` or `--expiring=false` | Yes, with a deprecation warning |
| Changed, `expiring_credentials: disabled` | No |
| Changed, disabled configuration and `--no-expiring=false` | Yes |

With a refreshable response, I saw `Received expiring refreshable token` and found the refresh token stored in the isolated configuration. With a non-expiring response, the base logged in without a token-type warning. The changed default printed `Host did not issue an expiring refreshable token` and still logged in.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

Explicit configuration opt-outs still work. `--no-expiring=false` overrides them. The host still decides which token type to issue.

Token paste remains available, including with deprecated `--expiring`. `--with-token` still stores the supplied token. `auth refresh` preserves the current token type unless its existing `--expiring` flag overrides it. The obsolete login hint is removed.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

Start with login's flag handling and the shared authentication-method choice. The manual walkthroughs now use the default token preference and select browser login with `--web`.

I ran `go fix ./internal/config ./pkg/cmd/auth/login ./pkg/cmd/auth/shared ./pkg/cmd/config/list` (passed) and `go test ./...` (passed). I ran `make lint` with the pinned v2.15.0 linter (passed). `bash -n script/refreshable-token-e2e.sh` and `bash -n script/refreshable-token-gitcredential-e2e.sh` both passed. I did not run the live walkthroughs.

### Authorship and follow-up

<!--
REQUIRED - If you are an AI agent filling in this template, answer "Who wrote this" for yourself and answer honestly. For "Who answers review comments," use only a choice the human has explicitly made in the conversation. If no choice has already been established, pause and ask the human to choose one of the three options before creating or updating the pull request. Do not infer the choice from repository ownership, authorship, assignees, prior interactions, or the current operator. After the human answers, check exactly the option they chose; the last option is valid when the human explicitly chooses nobody.

Check exactly one box in each list.
-->

Who wrote this:

- [ ] A human wrote it.
- [ ] An agent wrote it under close human direction.
- [x] An agent wrote it independently, and no human has guided the implementation beyond the initial prompt.

Who answers review comments:

- [x] @dev6 will read and reply directly.
- [ ] An agent will draft replies and @dev6 will read them before they are posted.
- [ ] Nobody has explicitly committed to replying.

### 🔵 Needs a closer look The supplied context does not establish maintainer approval for the non-interactive default change and removal of --expiring=false semantics. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR Makes expiring, refreshable credentials the default preference for `gh auth login`, using the existing token-refresh support while preserving configuration opt-outs and supplied-token authentication. **Changes:** - Enables `expiring_credentials` by default and adds `--no-expiring`, with explicit `false` overriding configuration opt-outs. - Deprecates login’s `--expiring` flag as a no-op, including `--expiring=false`, while keeping token paste available. - Updates help, tests, and manual walkthroughs for the new default and browser-login selection. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `script/​refreshable-token-gitcredential-e2e.sh` | Uses the default token preference and `--web`; updates helper-selection guidance. | | `script/​refreshable-token-e2e.sh` | Exercises default token requests with explicit browser login. | | `pkg/​cmd/​config/​list/​list_test.go` | Expects the enabled configuration default. | | `pkg/​cmd/​auth/​shared/​login_flow.go` | Removes forced browser login tied to explicit expiring-token requests. | | `pkg/​cmd/​auth/​shared/​login_flow_test.go` | Updates default-preference and authentication-method coverage. | | `pkg/​cmd/​auth/​shared/​git_credential.go` | Adjusts prompt wording and comments for default expiring-token requests. | | `pkg/​cmd/​auth/​login/​login.go` | Adds opt-out flag handling, deprecates the old flag, and updates help. | | `pkg/​cmd/​auth/​login/​login_test.go` | Covers flag compatibility, preference overrides, fallback, and refreshable storage. | | `internal/​config/​config.go` | Enables the default preference in configuration templates and metadata. |
Review effort: Balanced

title: Default to expiring login tokens
